To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the planning approach should be contingent upon the degree of environmental uncertainty and the confidence with which the causal linkages between the environment and the firm's actions can be determined.

(1) the planning process is a function of the degree of certainty about the causal linkages in a firm’s business environment, and (2) the planning process should be a function of the extent of change in the business environment.
(a) The planning approach used should be contingent upon the degree of environmental change and the degree of confidence in causal relationships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory that will help managers understand the conditions that require the use of different planning approaches.
the conditions under which different planning styles are appropriate and with how planning styles can be related to leadership and decision-making approaches.
the development of a planning framework and the implications of the framework for planning systems, leadership, and decision making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no definitive answers to the planning problem.
the appropriate planning approach is contingent on the conditions of the firm, and that there is no single best planning approach for all conditions.
the appropriate planning approach is dependent on the situation and is a function of the confidence in the causal relationships and the rate of environmental change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most appropriate planning system is the one that is best adapted to the situation at hand.
the most effective planning systems will be the ones that are most appropriate to the situation.
the planning system should be tailored to the business unit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the planning system should reflect the level of uncertainty in the environment.
there is no single planning approach that works best under all circumstances.
planning systems are not one-size-fits-all, but rather are contingent on a firm’s environment and the nature of its business.
